text:
Consider the nuclear fission

$Ne^{20}$ $\to$ $2He^{4} + C^{12}$

Given that the binding energy/ nucleon of $Ne^{20}$, He$^{4}$  and $C^{12}$ are, respectively, 8.03 MeV, 7.07 MeV and 7.86 MeV, identify the correct statement -
options: energy of 11.9 MeV has to be supplied
energy of 12.4 MeV will be supplied
energy of 3.6 MeV will be released
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$Ne^{20}\to$  $2He^{4}  + C^{12}$

Q – value, $E_{B} = ($BE$)_{$react} $-$ (BE$)_{$product}

= (20 × 8.03) – ((2 × 7.07 × 4) + 7.86 × 12)

= 160.6 – 150.88 = 9.72 MeV

The products have less total binding energy than $Ne^{20}$, so this energy has to be supplied (the reaction absorbs energy).

With the values exactly as printed, 9.72 MeV matches none of the options. The official answer is (B), energy of 11.9 MeV has to be supplied: the actual binding energy/nucleon of $C^{12}$ is 7.68 MeV (printed as 7.86 MeV in the paper), and with it

E = (20 × 8.03) – ((2 × 7.07 × 4) + 7.68 × 12) = 160.6 – (56.56 + 92.16) = 11.88 ≈ 11.9 MeV, which has to be supplied.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Evening Slot

text:
A metal plate of area 1 $\times$ $10^{–4} m^{2}$ is illuminated by a radiation of intensity $16 mW/m^{2}$. The work function of the metal is 5 eV. The energy of the incident photons is 10 eV and only 10% of it produces photo electrons.
The number of emitted photoelectrons per second and their maximum energy, respectively, will be
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that the area of the metal plate $A=1\times 10^{-4}m^{2}$, and the intensity of the radiation 

$I=16mW/m^{2}=16\times 10^{-3}W/m^{2}$.

The power $P$ falling on the metal plate is given by the product of the intensity of the radiation and the area:

$P=IA=(16\times 10^{-3}W/m^{2})(1\times 10^{-4}m^{2})=1.6\times 10^{-6}W$.

The energy of each incident photon is given as 10 eV. Converting this to joules (since 1 eV = $1.6\times 10^{-19}J$):

$E_{\text{photon}}=10eV=10\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}J=1.6\times 10^{-18}J$.

The number of incident photons per second $n_{\text{photon}}$ is then given by the total power divided by the energy per photon:

$n_{\text{photon}}=P/E_{\text{photon}}=1.6\times 10^{-6}W/1.6\times 10^{-18}J=10^{12}\text{photons/s}$.

Given that only 10% of these photons actually produce photoelectrons, the number of photoelectrons produced per second $n_{\text{electron}}$ is:

$n_{\text{electron}}=0.1\times n_{\text{photon}}=0.1\times 10^{12}=10^{11}\text{electrons/s}$.

The work function of the metal is given as 5 eV, which is the energy required to remove an electron from the metal. Therefore, the maximum energy of the photoelectrons $E_{\text{\max }}$ is given by the energy of the incident photons minus the work function:

$E_{\text{\max }}=E_{\text{photon}}-\text{Work function}=10eV-5eV=5eV$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Evening Slot

text: The diameter and height of a cylinder are measured by a meter scale to be 12.6 $\pm$ 0.1 cm and 34.2 $\pm$ 0.1 cm, respectively. What will be the value of its volume in appropriate significant figures ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$V=\frac{πd^{2}h}{4}=\frac{π\times (12.6)^{2}\times 34.2}{4}=4264.4\text{cm}^{3}$

$\frac{\Delta V}{V}=2\frac{\Delta d}{d}+\frac{\Delta h}{h}=2\times \frac{0.1}{12.6}+\frac{0.1}{34.2}=0.0159+0.0029=0.0188$

$\Delta V=0.0188\times 4264.4\approx 80\text{cm}^{3}$

Both measured values have three significant figures, so the volume is reported to three significant figures, $4260\text{cm}^{3}$, with the uncertainty in the same (tens) place: $V=(4260\pm 80)\text{cm}^{3}$. Rounding to $4300$ would discard the tens digit that the uncertainty still resolves.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th January Evening Slot

text: A parallel plate capacitor having capacitance 12 pF is charged by a battery to a potential difference of 10 V between its plates.
